 2–3. The comparison of the dead to dry leaves is a classical commonplace; e.g. Iliad vi 146–49; Aeneid vi
305–12. Cp. also Dante, Inferno iii 112–17; Paradise Lost i 300–303; Byron, Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage
iv 846; Q Mab v 4–6 and nn; L&C 162 and n. In a letter to Peacock of 23–24 January 1819 describing
the tombs at Pompeii, which the Shelleys visited on 23 December 1818, S. wrote: ‘The wild woods
surround them on either side . . . you hear the late leaves of autumn shiver & rustle in the stream of the
inconstant wind as it were like the step of ghosts’ (L ii 74). The leaves–ghosts analogy figures in PU II i
